voxel.title: Voxel
voxel.option.enabled.tooltip: Master activation toggle for the Voxel LOD engine. When active, distant world geometry is dynamically captured into compressed sparse voxel octrees and rendered directly on the GPU. Toggling it reloads the renderer on Apply.
voxel.option.worker_threads.tooltip: Recommended: %s threads on this CPU (%s logical threads, supported maximum %s). More threads speed up LOD generation but leave less CPU headroom for the game and shader pipeline.
voxel.option.share_sodium_threads.toolti: Coordinates background worker tasks with Sodium's chunk mesher pool, minimizing CPU cache thrashing and eliminating micro-stutters during high-speed exploration.
voxel.option.world_sampling.tooltip: Enables real-time capture and compression of newly generated or modified Minecraft chunks into persistent LOD voxel octrees as you traverse the world.
voxel.option.vram_budget.tooltip: Simple version: this limits how much VRAM distant terrain may use. The slider shows one buffer, and the game allocates a second identical buffer for light/AO, so total usage is about 2x the shown value. Suggested: 4 GB GPU = 512 MB/buffer (~1 GB total), 8 GB = 1024 MB (~2 GB), 12 GB = 1536 MB (~3 GB), 16 GB or more = 2048 MB (~4 GB). Too high can fight shaders/other mods for VRAM and cause stutter or crashes; too low can leave far terrain incomplete. Auto picks a safe value for your GPU; press Apply to take effect.
voxel.option.f3_diagnostics.tooltip: Shows a compact LOD summary on the F3 screen: active pipeline, geometry/VRAM usage, work queues, and frame timings. Detailed traversal counters remain in the periodic log dump. It costs a per-frame GPU readback, so enable it for debugging only. Apply reloads the renderer automatically.
voxel.option.performance_metrics.tooltip: Records frame-time percentiles, barrier/wait counters, upload/download bytes and mesh/storage stalls. Use /vx perf start, /vx perf stop and /vx perf dump to capture and export a scenario. Off by default.
voxel.option.rendering.tooltip: Enables GPU-driven drawing of distant voxel terrain. Disabling stops rasterization to save GPU power while background data sampling and octree caching remain active. Takes effect immediately on Apply.
voxel.option.mesh_precision.tooltip: Screen-space pixel threshold before subdividing octree nodes into finer geometry. Ultra and Balanced settings render sharper terrain features at the cost of higher GPU raster load, while Performance maximizes framerate.
voxel.option.horizon_distance.tooltip: Maximum horizontal visibility radius for distant LOD terrain in chunks (e.g., 16 sections = 512 chunks / ~8 kilometers of rendered landscape).
voxel.option.seam_overlap.tooltip: Geometric overlap margin between vanilla chunk borders and distant LOD meshes. A setting of 1-2 chunks eliminates visible seam cracks and prevents chunk pop-in during flight.
voxel.option.atmospheric_fog.tooltip: Seamlessly harmonizes distant LOD terrain with biome atmospheric colors and vanilla horizon fog, producing a unified natural horizon. Apply reloads the renderer automatically.
voxel.option.shader_shadows.tooltip: Extends sunlight attenuation, cloud shadows, and ambient shading from Beryl shaders across distant LOD landscapes.
voxel.option.water_ssr.tooltip: Renders real-time Screen-Space Reflections (SSR) and dynamic wave normal highlights on distant oceans, rivers, and water bodies. Apply reloads the renderer automatically.
voxel.option.sub_division.tooltip: Edge length (in blocks) of the finest LOD section. Larger values cut quad count and GPU cost in exchange for chunkier silhouettes.
voxel.option.adaptive_lod.tooltip: When the frame rate drops (for example while looking across a large vista), temporarily coarsen the far LOD above the configured sub-division size. It returns to the configured value when the view stabilises; this is a performance/quality trade-off and can cause visible LOD changes.
voxel.option.lod_scale.tooltip: Internal render resolution of the distant LOD pass as a percentage of the window. Lower values save a lot of GPU time but soften far terrain.
voxel.option.gpu_timing.tooltip: Debug only: writes Vulkan timestamps around each LOD pass and reads them back every 15 frames. Bottom-of-pipe timestamps can serialise passes, so keep it off while playing.
